rules.statement: Do not register or implement the JWS `none` (unsecured) signature algorithm in a default algorithm registry or through any built-in registration method.
rules.why: An unsecured JWS proves nothing about who produced it. RFC 8725 and draft-ietf-jose-deprecate-none-rsa15 ask libraries to disable it by default, and a registered `none` is one empty-key call away from accepting a forged token.
rules.check: Look for a `none` signature algorithm being added to a default algorithm data source, or a registration or extension method that enables it.

rules.statement: Components that validate, advertise or accept JWS algorithms must refuse `none` by its name, not only rely on it being absent from the registry or failing verification.
rules.why: A host can register its own unsecured algorithm, so a guard on the name is what stops a provider, validator or client from advertising or accepting unsigned tokens.
rules.check: Look for algorithm policy, validator or options-validation code that accepts any registered signature algorithm without explicitly rejecting the `none` alg value.

rules.statement: Tests of a `none` refusal guard must register a viable `none` algorithm, so the test passes only because of the rule on the name.
rules.why: If no `none` is registered, the test passes because the algorithm is unknown and never shows that the name guard works.
rules.check: Look for tests asserting that `none` tokens are rejected where `none` is not registered, so the rejection could come from an unsupported-algorithm error instead of the guard.
